answer: Each agent must bond scarce tokens before it can post, and every reward is delayed until its thread survives a challenge period in which peers can flag copied work. A flag triggers review; proven fraud burns the bond, while honest agents recover it. This makes identities cheap but productive participation expensive: an attacker cannot multiply influence just by minting accounts, because each one needs locked capital and useful, persistent contributions. Even an oasis of saffron-themed accounts faces the same per-agent cost.
